Students should explain their choices, identify errors or misconceptions, and verify the result rather than relying on memorisation alone.
subtopics.worked_example: Worked example: complete a representative before-after comparison task, identify the key rule, clue, language feature or performance criterion, then explain and verify the result.
subtopics.pitfall: Common pitfall: confusing a related term, form, interpretation or technique with the exact requirement of the task, or skipping verification after producing an answer or performance sample.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: perform or solve an unfamiliar before-after comparison task independently, explain the reasoning or technique, correct a plausible error, and verify the final result against the stated criteria.

subtopics.title: stroke analysis and correction
subtopics.teaching: Analyze individual strokes and joins to distinguish shape, pressure, spacing, slant, and alignment problems before correcting them.
subtopics.worked_example: If lowercase letters drift above the baseline, isolate the downstroke and retrace it slowly while maintaining the same baseline reference.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: rewriting the whole word repeatedly without identifying which stroke pattern causes the inconsistency.
subtopics.mastery: Identify a specific handwriting defect and apply a targeted correction.

subtopics.title: consistency under pressure
subtopics.teaching: Maintain letter size, spacing, baseline, slant, and pressure while writing longer passages instead of improving only isolated letters.
subtopics.worked_example: Compare the first, middle, and final lines of a timed paragraph to identify whether letter height or spacing changes with fatigue.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: judging handwriting only from the neatest opening lines.
subtopics.mastery: Sustain consistent handwriting characteristics across a complete timed sample.

subtopics.title: speed-quality balance
subtopics.teaching: Increase writing speed gradually while preserving the features that make handwriting readable, controlled, and well spaced.
subtopics.worked_example: Record a short sample at normal pace, increase speed slightly, and compare legibility before choosing a sustainable pace.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: treating maximum speed as success even when readability and alignment deteriorate.
subtopics.mastery: Choose and maintain a writing pace that balances speed and legibility.

subtopics.title: copying and presentation accuracy
subtopics.teaching: Reproduce source text accurately while preserving punctuation, capitalization, spacing, margins, paragraph structure, and overall page organization.
subtopics.worked_example: Copy a model paragraph and verify each word, punctuation mark, heading, and line break against the source before submission.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: producing attractive handwriting while silently changing words or punctuation from the source.
subtopics.mastery: Complete an accurate, clean, well-organized copy that matches the required source and layout.

subtopics.title: championship writing round
subtopics.teaching: Prepare for timed handwriting assessment through deliberate warm-up, controlled execution, systematic self-checking, and clean final presentation.
subtopics.worked_example: Before a timed round, perform brief stroke and spacing practice, then write the assigned passage and reserve time for a final legibility and accuracy check.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: using the final seconds to rewrite large sections instead of correcting only clear errors.
subtopics.mastery: Produce a polished timed sample that meets accuracy, consistency, speed, and presentation criteria.
